key_points: Derive distinct observable predictions from ecological modernization vs durable inequality rather than an IRA periodization
Frame composition vs within-occupation as allocation vs pay-setting processes
Map subtypes onto theorized dimensions (legacy/utility vs new/merchant)
Use detailed SOC rows only (proposal mixes aggregation levels)
Cluster on detailed occupation; occupation x year FE
Primary contrast non-overlapping estimate windows; deflate wages
Pool geothermal and biomass; precision-weight robustness; report cell counts
Add interindustry wage differential and establishment pay literature
Soften absolute novelty claim; frame as descriptive benchmark for just transition
Bundle as one argument: is renewable generation a good-jobs transition?
Address OEWS time-series caveat and generation-only NAICS scope explicitly
Adjacent May estimates share two-thirds of panels; compare non-overlapping windows
Balanced fixed-occupation panel to separate publication changes from real change
Subtype-by-year convergence for tiny subtypes would be a fatal flaw - avoid

cross_agent_agreement: (5/5) Fix SOC aggregation double counting; detailed occupations only
(4/5) OEWS 3-year pooling: use non-overlapping May 2021 vs May 2024 windows as primary trend contrast; describe as persistence not IRA effect
(4/5) Pool or flag geothermal/biomass; no subtype convergence claims
consensus: mixed-to-strong: bundle RQ-A (headline) + RQ-C (core heterogeneity) + RQ-B (bridging decomposition); RQ-D robustness
